question: Which protocol resolves host names to IP addresses?

evidence.clue: cannot open the intranet by its name
evidence.why: Only the name fails, which points at the step that turns names into addresses.

evidence.clue: the same site opens by its IP address
evidence.why: The path to the server works. Only the name-to-address step is broken.

evidence.clue: the server address could not be found
evidence.why: This message means the name lookup got no answer.

evidence.tap: Their IP address and gateway look correct
evidence.why: Good addressing rules out DHCP and gateway faults. It points away from them, not toward the answer.

evidence.tap: It is the third call this week
evidence.why: How often it happens does not tell you what is broken.

question: Which pair of devices sends a signal down every wire, one by one, to confirm a cable was wired to the right pins?

evidence.clue: put new plugs on both ends of a patch cord
evidence.why: A cord with fresh plugs is the thing to check before it goes into use.

evidence.tap: the user comes back from lunch
evidence.why: When the user returns says nothing about the tool.

evidence.clue: confirm each wire lands on the right pin
evidence.why: Checking every pin from one end to the other is what this tool is for.

evidence.clue: plug one part into each end
evidence.why: This tool comes as a pair: one part sends, the other shows each wire in turn.

evidence.clue: watch the lights step through 1 to 8
evidence.why: The lights show the signal reaching each pin, one by one.

evidence.tap: The cord will later join a bundle in the closet
evidence.why: Finding one cable in a bundle is the toner probe's job, not this one.

question: Which tool puts a tone on a cable so you can find it in an unlabeled bundle?

evidence.why: The room temperature has nothing to do with the tool.

evidence.clue: forty cables hang with no labels
evidence.why: An unlabeled bundle is the problem this tool solves.

evidence.clue: find which one runs to Room 12
evidence.why: The job is to trace one cable, not to test it.

evidence.clue: clip a small box onto the cable at the Room 12 jack
evidence.why: That box puts the tone on the cable.

evidence.clue: move a wand along the bundle, listening
evidence.why: The wand picks up the tone to find the right cable.

evidence.tap: Later each wire must go to the right pin
evidence.why: Checking pins is a cable tester's job, a different tool.

question: What does Windows call it when a host picks itself a 169.254.x.x address because no DHCP server answered?

evidence.why: The day tells you nothing about how the address was set.

evidence: , a laptop is plugged into the office network but no web pages load. ipconfig shows

evidence.clue: an address of 169.254.12.40
evidence.why: 169.254.x.x is the range Windows gives itself when it gets no lease.

evidence.clue: the address server was switched off
evidence.why: No DHCP server was there to answer. That is what sets off APIPA.

evidence.clue: no address was ever leased
evidence.why: The laptop never got a configuration, so it picked one for itself.

evidence.tap: link light on the port is green
evidence.why: A green light shows the cable works. It says nothing about how the address was set.

question: Which setting holds the router address a host uses to reach other networks?

evidence.clue: can print to the printer on its own subnet
evidence.why: Local traffic works, so the fault is only in leaving the subnet.

evidence.clue: cannot reach servers on other networks or the internet
evidence.why: Anything off the subnet needs the router, and the PC has no way to it.

evidence.tap: a valid IP address, a valid mask
evidence.why: These let it talk on its own network. They are fine here, so they are not the fault.

evidence.clue: a blank router entry
evidence.why: The router address is the missing setting.
Their start day says nothing about the setting.

question: Which internet connection has high latency because the signal goes to orbit and back?

evidence.clue: far from any phone or cable lines
evidence.why: No lines rules out DSL, cable and fiber, which leaves the wireless kinds.

evidence.clue: a dish aimed high at the sky
evidence.why: A dish pointed up, not at a nearby tower, is aimed at a satellite.
Good download speed fits many connection types, so it is not evidence for one.

evidence.clue: video calls lag almost a second
evidence.why: That much delay comes from the long trip to orbit and back.

question: Which twisted pair cable adds foil or braid to cope with motors and fluorescent lights nearby?
evidence: A factory needs a network cable run

evidence.clue: right beside large electric motors
evidence.why: Motors give off interference that can spoil the signal.

evidence.clue: dropped data whenever the machines started
evidence.why: Errors that follow the machines point at interference, not a broken cable.

evidence.clue: with foil around its twisted pairs
evidence.why: Foil or braid is the shielding that keeps the interference out.
40 m is well inside the limit for twisted pair, so the length decides nothing.

evidence.tap: It runs along the floor, not above the ceiling
evidence.why: An air space above the ceiling would call for plenum cable. This run is not in one, so it rules that out rather than pointing at the answer.

question: Which fire-safe cable must be used in the air-handling space above a false ceiling?
evidence: A tech will run new network cable

evidence.clue: above the drop ceiling
evidence.why: The space above a false ceiling is where the fire rule applies.

evidence.clue: Air for the heating system flows back through that space
evidence.why: An air-handling space spreads smoke through the building.

evidence.clue: the fire inspector will check the cable jacket
evidence.why: The rule is about what the jacket gives off when it burns.

evidence.tap: The run passes close to fluorescent lights
evidence.why: Lights cause interference, which calls for shielding (STP). They do not decide the fire rating.

evidence.tap: The job is due by Friday
evidence.why: The deadline says nothing about the cable type.
